applicableAreas: Site plan, Electrical design plan - all proposed buildings
findings.observation: Reviewed Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) which shows 8 proposed buildings (Bldg. 1-8). Vision analysis confirms that meters are depicted on the buildings with generic 'Electrical Meters' labels, and transformers are shown as 'Electrical Transformer Pad' callouts. However, the plan does not clearly indicate the power source (service voltage, amperage, or service type) for any of the proposed buildings. The vision tool response explicitly states: 'No, projected electrical loads (kW, kVA, or amperage) are not shown anywhere on this sheet.' While the sheet shows where meters and transformers will be located graphically, there is no accompanying text, table, or note identifying the service voltage, service type (primary/secondary), or how each building will be powered.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(5) requires that plans show 'Power source for proposed buildings' as part of the application requirements for Austin Energy land development review. The grouping's Regulatory Overview states that 'Point of service identified with one service voltage' must be shown on plans (item #7 under Plan Documentation Requirements). The vision analysis of Sheet 21 confirms no text or labels indicating service voltage, amperage, or service type for the proposed buildings. While the physical locations of meters and transformers are graphically depicted, without identification of the power source (voltage level and capacity), the requirement to show 'power source for proposed buildings' is not met. This is distinct from EL-10.8 (proposed facilities shown) because the facilities themselves may be shown, but their functional designation as power source is missing.
findings.comment: Proposed power source and service specifications (voltage, amperage, service type) not identified for proposed buildings. Specify the service voltage (primary/secondary), amperage, and service type (single/three-phase) for each building or building group on the electrical design plan.

applicableAreas: Electrical design plan - service connection point
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows the proposed electrical infrastructure on the site, including transformers, pull boxes, meters, and underground electric lines connecting buildings. Vision analysis confirms that the sheet displays 'Electrical Transformer Pad' (multiple locations near buildings), 'Underground Electric Line' routing, and 'Electrical Meters' on building exteriors. However, the plan does not show the point where the proposed electrical system connects to existing Austin Energy (AE) facilities. The vision analysis notes that 'OHE' (overhead electric) lines are shown along property boundaries as existing facilities, but there is no labeled callout or note indicating where proposed conduit or service lines connect to the existing AE infrastructure. The sheet lacks any annotation, dimension, or diagram showing the actual connection point to the existing utility lines.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(5) explicitly requires plans to show 'Point of service identified with one service voltage.' The Regulatory Overview clarifies that 'Point of service identifies the demarcation between Austin Energy-owned infrastructure and customer-owned facilities.' Without a clear point of connection shown on the plans, there is no way to determine where the demarcation occurs, which infrastructure is AE-owned vs. customer-owned, or whether the proposed service configuration complies with AE policy requiring one point of service per lot. This is a critical documentation requirement for AE review and cannot be assessed from the available plans.
findings.comment: Point of service connection to existing Austin Energy infrastructure not shown on plans. Identify and label the specific connection point to the existing AE electrical system, showing the demarcation between AE-owned and customer-owned facilities.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows underground electric lines (blue solid lines with callout box labeled 'Underground Electric Line') connecting transformers and pull boxes to building meter locations. However, the vision analysis confirms that while these lines show internal site routing between proposed equipment, there is no indication of how the service enters the site or connects from the existing AE facilities at the property boundary to the proposed transformers and meters. The plan shows internal site electric routing but does not trace the service path from the point where it would connect to existing AE infrastructure (shown as 'OHE' lines and poles near property boundaries) to the proposed transformer pads and distribution points on the site.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(5) requires plans to show 'Approximate location and space for electric facilities, desired service point, projected load shown' and specifically requires documentation of 'Proposed electrical route from existing AE service to proposed service.' This requirement ensures that the applicant has coordinated with AE regarding the service entrance location, the routing path, and any required conduit or ductwork. Without this routing shown, it is unclear whether the service can physically reach the proposed transformer locations, whether it conflicts with site improvements, or whether adequate space and clearances exist. The absence of service routing from existing to proposed facilities prevents verification of the overall service design completeness.
findings.comment: Proposed electrical service routing from existing Austin Energy infrastructure to proposed service not shown. Clearly show the routing path for the service entrance, including conduit sizing, length, and routing details from the point of connection to the proposed transformer locations.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows electrical transformers, pull boxes, meters, and underground electric lines. Vision analysis of the sheet indicates that transformers are labeled generically as 'Electrical Transformer Pad' and meters are labeled as 'Electrical Meters' with no additional designation. There are no notes, labels, or callouts indicating whether the service is primary (supplied directly from AE distribution), secondary (from a customer transformer), or specifying the voltage level of the service. The overhead electric lines shown as existing ('OHE') and the proposed underground service have no voltage designations. UCM § 1.3.3 requires that service be identified as primary or secondary, and no such designation appears on the electrical design plan.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.3 'One Point of Service and One Service Voltage' establishes that plans must identify whether the service is primary (customer receives service at AE's distribution voltage, typically 12.47kV) or secondary (customer receives service at utilization voltage, typically 120/208V or 277/480V via a customer-owned transformer). This designation is fundamental to understanding the service configuration and AE's scope of work vs. customer responsibility. Without this identification, AE cannot determine whether proposed equipment (transformers, metering) is correctly specified, whether clearances are adequate for the service voltage, and whether the service aligns with AE policy. The omission of primary vs. secondary designation prevents verification of compliance with UCM § 1.3.3.
findings.comment: Service voltage not identified as primary or secondary. Specify on the electrical design plan whether the service is primary voltage (AE-supplied) or secondary voltage (customer-owned transformer), and label the service voltage on all applicable facilities and lines.

findings.observation: Reviewed Sheet 1 (Cover Sheet) by reading the full blocks.md content for all administrative, boilerplate, and notes sections. The cover sheet contains extensive notes including: fire department requirements (Block 7), recycling ordinance (Block 15), drainage maintenance (Block 14), Edwards Aquifer note (Block 22), and other utility/environmental notes. General electrical notes appear on Sheet 3 (Block 8: 'Electric Notes' with 5 items regarding Austin Energy tree work and easements, and Block 14 with similar content, and Block 20 with 16 Electric Transmission Notes). However, the Cover Sheet (Sheet 1) contains no section titled 'AE Standard Notes' or 'Austin Energy Standard Notes.' The electrical transmission notes on Sheet 3 are present but do not constitute the standard AE Standard Notes required for all site plans. These notes address transmission line work and safety but are not comprehensive standard notes covering electric service design, clearances, easements, plat requirements, and other standard AE documentation requirements.
findings.reasoning: The grouping's Regulatory Overview (line 40) explicitly states: 'Required Plat Notes (UCM § 1.16.0(8)): When plats are recorded as part of land development approval, specific Austin Energy notes must appear on the plat.' While plat notes are specifically for recorded plats, the checklist item EL-10.19 cites 'Reviewer Convention' which establishes that AE Standard Notes should be present on all site plans to provide standard language regarding Austin Energy's rights, owner responsibilities, and required practices. The cover sheet is the standard location for such notes. The presence of general electrical transmission notes on Sheet 3 does not satisfy the requirement for comprehensive AE Standard Notes covering all aspects of electric service design, easement management, and utility coordination.
findings.comment: Austin Energy Standard Notes not provided on plans. Include comprehensive AE Standard Notes on the cover sheet covering easement access, tree work, clearance maintenance, and other standard Austin Energy requirements for electric service and infrastructure.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) is reviewed for the presence of a note stating that all electric infrastructure (existing and proposed) is shown on the plan or noting exceptions requiring AE pre-approval. The vision analysis of Sheet 21 explicitly confirms: 'No, there is no note at the top or anywhere else on the sheet with that specific phrasing or similar language indicating completeness of the electric infrastructure shown.' The sheet contains general utility notes (Block 6 on the blocks.md states 'Contractor shall verify horizontal and vertical location of existing utilities' and disclaimers about existing utility locations). However, there is no affirmative statement indicating that all existing and proposed electric infrastructure requiring approval has been shown on the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan, nor any notation of exceptions that require separate AE approval.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1) requires that plans show 'All existing electric facilities (transmission/distribution structures, guys, anchors, transformers)' and 'All existing and proposed permanent structures' and 'Sufficient clearances demonstrated for existing and proposed electric facilities.' Without a note stating that all infrastructure is shown (or exceptions noted), reviewers cannot determine whether missing elements are intentional omissions subject to later AE approval or unintentional oversights. The Regulatory Overview section lists common violation patterns: 'Missing plat note requirements' and identifies that the grouping addresses 'what must be shown on plans to demonstrate a complete electric design.' A note confirming completeness or documenting exceptions is essential to that completeness demonstration. The title 'Preliminary Electrical Design Plan' suggests the design is not yet final, but even preliminary submissions must include a note about completeness or noted exceptions.
findings.comment: Note missing stating all electric infrastructure shown and exceptions require AE pre-approval. Add a note to the electrical design plan stating: 'All existing and proposed electric infrastructure required for service to this project is shown on this plan, except where noted separately or subject to Austin Energy Design approval.'

applicableAreas: Plans showing electrical easements - Site Plan (Sheet 9), Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21), Plat (Sheet 2), Landscape Plan (Sheet 31), Grading Plan (Sheet 11)
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 2 (Plat) vision analysis: Easements are shown with width dimensions (5' P.U.E., 5' Elec. & Tel. Easement, 5' Elec. Easement) but the vision analysis explicitly states: 'No. The labels on the plat do not contain the words "aerial," "overhead," or "underground."' Sheet 21 vision analysis confirms: 'Existing easements are shown (as noted above). However, the labels do not explicitly distinguish between "aerial" or "underground" within the easement text itself (they are generally labeled "P.U.E." or "Elec. & Tele. Easement"). The lines running through or near some of these easements are labeled "OHE" (Overhead Electric), implying aerial use in those specific areas, but the easement labels themselves do not make this distinction.' Sheet 9 vision analysis notes: '5' Electric Easement is labeled along the right (eastern) property boundary' and '5' Elec. & Tele. Easement labeled near the bottom right' but no distinction of type. Both aerial (overhead conductors, poles, service drops, guy wires) and underground (conduit, pad-mounted transformers) electric infrastructure exist on this site. The regulatory overview explicitly distinguishes these: 'Aerial electric easements accommodate overhead facilities... with vertical sky-to-ground clearance requirements; non-aerial easements accommodate underground facilities... with horizontal and subsurface clearance requirements.' Without this distinction labeled on easements, plan reviewers cannot verify that clearances and access are adequate for the actual facility type using each easement.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1)(i) requires plans to show 'All public and private easements (electrical, gas, water, sewer, telecommunications, drainage) with locations and extents clearly delineated.' The grouping's Code References section (lines 72-90) identifies UCM § 1.10.3 and § 1.10.4 as establishing different clearance requirements for aerial vs. non-aerial easements. The Regulatory Overview specifically states: 'Plans must distinguish between: Aerial vs. Non-Aerial Easements: Aerial electric easements accommodate overhead facilities (poles, overhead conductors, service drops, guy wires) with vertical sky-to-ground clearance requirements (7.5 ft horizontal, 15-ft radius); non-aerial easements accommodate underground facilities (conduit, pad-mounted transformers, underground laterals).' Without this distinction labeled on the plans themselves, it is impossible to verify that clearances meet requirements for the type of facility in each easement. Both overhead and underground facilities are shown on this site (OHE lines on Sheet 21, underground conduits on Sheet 21), confirming that both easement types exist.
findings.comment: Electrical easements not distinguished as aerial vs. underground. Label all electrical easements to specify whether they accommodate aerial facilities (overhead poles, conductors, guy wires) or underground facilities (conduits, pad-mounted equipment, buried laterals), and ensure clearance requirements are applied appropriately to each type.

applicableAreas: All sheets showing electrical easements - Plat (Sheet 2), Site Plan (Sheet 9), Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21), and others
findings.observation: Sheet 2 (Plat) vision analysis explicitly confirms: 'No. While there are volume and page references shown on the plat (in circles indicating adjacent property deed records, e.g., Vol. 3058 Pg. 2327), there are no specific Volume/Page references or document numbers attached directly to the easement labels themselves. The labels only indicate if they are "(Exist.)" or "(Existing)."' Sheet 21 vision analysis confirms easements are shown with labels like '5' Elec. & Tele. Easement Vol. 5468, Pg. 385 D.R.T.C.Tx.' (which does have recording info on this sheet), but upon closer examination, sheet 9 shows '5' Electric Easement' and '5' Elec. & Tele. Easement' with no volume/page references shown. The facts.md document (lines 135-143) identifies several existing electric easements: '5' Electric Easements (×2)' with 'Document Ref: Travis County Doc 73/76, Case C8S-75-160' and '7.5' Public Utility Easement' with the same reference. These recorded documents should be cited on the plans. On Sheet 2, the plat does not include volume/page references for the electric easement labels, representing an omission of required recording information.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1)(i) requires easements to be shown 'with locations and extents clearly delineated.' The term 'clearly delineated' encompasses not only spatial location and width but also legal identification. The Regulatory Overview explicitly states: 'Recording information: Electric infrastructure documentation requirements... UCM § 1.16.0 serves as the comprehensive baseline for land development review applications, specifying what must be shown on plans to obtain Austin Energy approval.' LDC § 25-4-132 (cited in Code References) requires 'Easement dimensions, locations, and designations to match exactly between plat and site plan.' Without recording information (volume/page or document number), easement locations cannot be verified against recorded documents, overlapping or conflicting easements cannot be identified, and the legal identity of each easement is unclear. This is particularly important where multiple easements may exist on the same site (this site has at least 7-9 documented easements per facts.md). Recording information must appear on all plan sheets showing easements.
findings.comment: Recording information (volume/page, document number, or plat reference) not provided for existing electrical easements. Add recording information to all easement labels, cross-referencing the Travis County plat or deed document where the easement was recorded (e.g., 'Vol. 73, Pg. 76, Case C8S-75-160').

applicableAreas: Site Plan (Sheet 9), Utility Plan (Sheet 21), Landscape Plan (Sheet 31), Grading Plan (Sheet 11)
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) vision analysis confirms: 'Transformer Pad (Typ.) is explicitly shown and labeled on the west side... Individual meters, pull boxes, and detailed underground electrical conduits routing to the specific buildings are not visibly drawn or labeled on this sheet.' Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) shows comprehensive electrical facilities (transformers, pull boxes, meters, underground lines) with explicit labels. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) vision analysis states: 'There are no clear labels or specific symbols explicitly identifying electrical facilities such as transformers, meters, or pull boxes on this landscape plan sheet.' Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) guide mentions 'utility easements' but vision analysis reveals electrical infrastructure details are not shown there. The grouping's Documents to Review section (lines 94-103) specifies: 'Verify all electric facilities and easements shown consistently across sheets' and lists 'Site Plan, Utility Plan, Landscape Plan, Grading Plan, Irrigation Plan' as required sheets. Detailed electrical facilities shown on Sheet 21 are not shown consistently on all other sheets where they should appear (particularly Landscape and Grading plans where transformer locations and clearances are critical).
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1) requires plans to show electric infrastructure, and the grouping's common violation patterns specifically identify: 'Cross-sheet inconsistency: Electric facilities shown on utility plan but omitted from landscape, grading, or irrigation plans where coordination is critical (especially down guy anchors conflicting with accessible paths, trees conflicting with clearance envelopes).' The principle is that all infrastructure must be consistently shown on all sheets where coordination is necessary. The Regulatory Overview states (line 54): 'Cross-sheet inconsistency: Electric facilities shown on utility plan but omitted from landscape, grading, or irrigation plans where coordination is critical.' This project shows detailed electrical design on Sheet 21 but lacks consistent electrical facility depiction on Landscape (Sheet 31) and Grading (Sheet 11) plans, preventing verification of clearances, coordination with other site features, and staging area adequacy.
findings.comment: Electric facilities not shown consistently across all required plan sheets. Show all proposed electric facilities (transformers, pull boxes, meters, underground conduit routing, easements) on Site Plan (Sheet 9), Landscape Plan (Sheet 31), and Grading Plan (Sheet 11) with consistent symbols and locations matching Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan).

applicableAreas: Landscape Plan (Sheet 31) - southern property boundary where overhead electric lines run
findings.observation: Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows overhead electric lines labeled 'OHE' running horizontally along the bottom (southern) edge of the site. Vision analysis explicitly confirms: 'Yes, overhead electric lines are shown. A line clearly labeled "---OHE---" runs horizontally along the bottom edge of the site plan. Regarding vegetation clearance, there does NOT appear to be clear clearance. Several proposed tree symbols (circles representing canopies) are drawn directly overlapping or immediately adjacent to the "OHE" line, particularly towards the bottom right section of the plan.' The Regulatory Overview (lines 61-64) establishes clearance requirements: 'Distribution facilities (<60kV, typically 12.47kV) with 15-foot radial clearances' and more specifically 'Permanent clearances from overhead distribution (UCM § 1.10.3): 7.5 feet minimum horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from overhead primary, neutral, secondary conductors; 15-foot radius clearance from overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors.' Trees directly adjacent to overhead lines violate this 15-foot radial clearance requirement.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires '15-foot radius clearance from overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors.' This is a safety clearance to prevent tree branches and fall hazards from contacting energized conductors. The grouping's Common Violation Patterns section (line 54) specifically identifies: 'trees conflicting with clearance envelopes' as a cross-sheet coordination problem. Vision analysis of Sheet 31 confirms trees are 'directly overlapping or immediately adjacent to the OHE line' rather than maintaining 15-foot separation. This represents a direct conflict between the landscape design (trees) and the electrical infrastructure (OHE lines with required 15-foot clearance). Sheet 21 shows the overhead electric lines exist on this site, and Sheet 31 landscape plan fails to maintain required clearance from those existing lines.
findings.comment: Tree locations not coordinated with overhead electric line clearances. Relocate all landscape plantings (particularly trees with mature canopies) to maintain minimum 15-foot radial clearance from the overhead electric (OHE) lines shown along the southern property boundary.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) is reviewed for the presence of projected electrical load information. Vision analysis explicitly confirms: 'No, projected electrical loads (kW, kVA, or amperage) are not shown anywhere on this sheet.' The sheet contains building square footage and finished floor elevations (e.g., 'Bldg. 1: 3,290 sf, FFE = 687.50'), but there is no statement of total project electrical load, load per building, service amperage, or any other load specification. The sheet title block designates it as 'Preliminary Electrical Design Plan' but contains no load calculations or specifications.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(6) explicitly requires that plans show 'Projected electrical load required for electric service' as part of the application requirements. The Regulatory Overview (lines 32-33) states that the plan documentation must show 'Approximate location and space for electric facilities, desired service point, projected load shown' as item #8 in the comprehensive baseline for applications. Projected load is essential information for Austin Energy to determine service requirements, transformer sizing, and capacity. Without projected load, AE cannot verify that the proposed transformer(s) are adequately sized, that conduit sizing is appropriate, or that the overall service design meets load demands.
findings.comment: Projected electrical load not shown on plans. Calculate and show the total electrical load for the project (in kW or kVA) and identify the load for each building or service point, based on building size, occupancy classification, and code-required minimum loads.
